rows.name: Hermon
rows.note: ⭐ "The last before the persecution in our day, succeeded to the apostolic chair, which has been preserved there until the present time." ⚠ Eusebius is writing about his own see's neighbour and still gives no year.

rows.name: Sophronius III
rows.note: ⛔ Hamilton lists him with the words "dates not known" and Pringle's table does not reach him. He is a NAME IN THE ORDER and nothing else, and that is exactly what the band should show. Placement between Athanasius II and Gregory I is Hamilton's ordering, not a date.

rows.name: James, the brother of the Lord
rows.note: ⭐⭐⭐ First of the fifteen bishops "of the circumcision" Eusebius names in order at HE IV.5.3, and the only one the band dates, because his death is fixed independently (ch. 2). ⚠ The other fourteen carry NO dates in any source Eusebius could find.

rows.name: Simeon son of Clopas
rows.note: Second. ⚠ Eusebius dates his martyrdom to Trajan's reign under the governor Atticus (ch. 4's spine row, c.107) -- one of only two or three of the fifteen to whom the Chronicle assigns any date at all. ⚠⚠ NOT the Symeon II of 1092-1099: they are a thousand years apart and the book must never let them collide.

rows.name: Justus
rows.note: Third. Eusebius's Chronicle refers his accession to the tenth year of Trajan (107); NPNF's editor notes this leaves THIRTEEN bishops for the years to 135, "which is, to say the least, very suspicious."

rows.name: Zacchaeus, Tobias, Benjamin, John, Matthias, Philip, Seneca, Justus, Levi, Ephres, Joseph, Judas
rows.note: ⭐⭐ Fourth to fifteenth, HE IV.5.3, GIVEN AS ONE ROW ON PURPOSE. Twelve names with no dates, no acts and no order beyond Eusebius's listing, ending at Hadrian's siege. Splitting them into twelve dated cells would manufacture a succession out of a list. ⚠ NPNF's editor: after Symeon's death "the presbyters took the lead, and they were afterward made by tradition into successive monarchical bishops"; Closs and Gieseler suppose bishops of several Palestinian churches at the SAME TIME, later strung into one Jerusalem line. ✅ ch. 4 already says this in its own words.

rows.name: Marcus
rows.note: ⭐⭐ THE HINGE: the first GENTILE bishop, after Hadrian's refoundation as Aelia Capitolina (HE IV.6, V.12.1). The church of the circumcision ends here and the see continues. No dates.

rows.name: Cassianus, Publius, Maximus, Julian, Gaius, Symmachus, Gaius II, Julian II, Capito, Maximus II, Valentinus, Valens, Dolichianus
rows.note: ⭐⭐ HE V.12.2, again ONE ROW. ⚠⚠ A TEXTUAL PROBLEM THE BAND MUST NOT SMOOTH: Eusebius says Narcissus was "the fifteenth in succession from the siege" and "the thirtieth from the apostles", but the list as transmitted gives only THIRTEEN names. The Chronicle and Epiphanius restore a second Maximus and a Valentinus between Capito and Valens, and NPNF's editor calls the omission a scribe's mistake. Those two are carried here IN THAT POSITION, on that reasoning, and the reasoning is why. ⚠ The Chronicle's dates for Cassianus (160) and Maximus II (185) are NOT used: "it is said in the Chron. itself that the dates of the various bishops are not known, and hence no reliance can be placed upon these figures."

rows.name: Narcissus
rows.note: ⭐ THE FIRST NAME IN THE WHOLE BAND WITH A DATE THAT IS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN TRADITION. Attested as bishop in the tenth year of Commodus, 189 (HE V.22 -- already ch. 5's spine row), presided at the Palestinian paschal council under Victor of Rome, alive after 212 in his 116th year, and dead before 216, since Alexander is bishop at Origen's visit. ⚠ NPNF: "The date of Narcissus' accession to the see of Jerusalem is not known to us." The END is inferred, the ATTESTATION is firm, so this is a point.

rows.name: Alexander
rows.note: ⭐ Kept at Jerusalem as coadjutor to the aged Narcissus when he arrived on pilgrimage (c.212), and died in prison at Caesarea in the Decian persecution -- both already ch. 6's spine rows. He founded the library at Jerusalem that Eusebius used. ⚠ The overlap with Narcissus is real and is not an error in the list: for a time there were two bishops in the city by arrangement.

rows.name: Mazabanes
rows.note: Named as Alexander's successor and nothing more. No dates in any source.

rows.name: Hymenaeus
rows.note: ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIRST NAME IN THE BAND WHOSE DATES THE APPARATUS DEFENDS RATHER THAN DISCLAIMS. NPNF n. 2287: the Chronicle expressly says the dates of the EARLIER Jerusalem bishops are unknown, "but with the dates of the bishops of the latter part of the third century Eusebius can hardly have been unacquainted, and that Hymenaeus was bishop at any rate as early as 265 is proved by chaps. 27 and 30" -- his presence at the Antiochian synods on Paul of Samosata. "The dates given in the Chron. may therefore be accepted as at least approximately correct." ⭐⭐ THE MECHANISM IS THE POINT AND IT RECURS: the succession becomes datable exactly when its holder starts appearing in OTHER PEOPLE'S dated business. Gil says the same of the Islamic centuries -- "we have to determine the times of these patriarchs' lives according to the events in which they were involved" -- 1,600 years apart and from the opposite end.

rows.name: Zambdas
rows.note: Succeeded Hymenaeus and "died in a short time".

rows.name: Macarius
rows.note: ⭐⭐ THE ONLY TWO-AUTHORITY ROW IN THE WHOLE BYZANTINE STRETCH, and it already sits in ch. 11's spine row: Di Segni gives 314-334, Hirschfeld ca. 314-333. The ends differ by a year and one is hedged, so it is a point. He received Constantine's letter ordering the basilica over the tomb (ch. 9).

rows.name: Maximus
rows.note: ⚠ ch. 8's spine row carries him at TIER V -- reported from Sozomen 2.20, whose synchronism the spine flags. He convened the synod that received Athanasius in 346 (ch. 8).

rows.name: Cyril
rows.note: ⭐ Consecrated 350 or early in 351, dying about 386, with Hunt putting the end of the episcopate at 387 -- the disagreement already recorded on the c.386 spine row. Deposed and exiled THREE TIMES between, under Acacius, at Constantinople and under Valens, returning for good in 378: four of the band's most eventful years are years he was not in the city. ⚠⚠ THE EXILES ARE WHY A BAR WOULD LIE HERE even if the ends agreed.

rows.name: Praylius
rows.note: ⚠ Recorded only because Pringle's Juvenal entry needs him: "Praylius began in 417 and did not last long." His own succession and end are not on this shelf.

rows.name: Juvenal
rows.note: ⭐⭐ THE HINGE OF THE WHOLE LANE: at Chalcedon in 451 Jerusalem is raised to a patriarchate and the bishop becomes a patriarch. Six of ch. 13's spine rows are his. His death is dated by Cyril of Scythopolis, Vit. Euth. 33 -- the same sentence that dates his successor.

rows.name: Anastasius
rows.note: Dated only by the sentence of Cyril of Scythopolis that dates Juvenal's death. No end on this shelf.

rows.name: Sallustius
rows.note: ⚠ THE DATES HERE ARE ATTESTATIONS, NOT A TENURE: he ordained Sabas priest on 12 December 491 and was dying in 494 when the monks assembled at him (both ch. 11 spine rows). The start of 486 is NOT on this shelf and is placement only.

rows.name: Elias
rows.note: ⭐ Dedicated the great church of the Theotokos at the Great Laura on 1 July 501; ousted by Anastasius on 1 September 516 and banished to Aila (ch. 13 spine rows). ⚠ The 494 start is placement, not evidence.

rows.name: John III
rows.note: John son of Marcianus, who promised to conform and did not; the dux of Palestine imprisoned him for breaking the promise and he was released after being coached by Zacharias (ch. 13's spine row).

rows.name: Zacharias
rows.note: ⭐⭐ Carried to Persia with the True Cross when the city fell in 614 (ch. 15's spine row). ⚠ The 609 start is placement, not evidence.

rows.name: Modestus
rows.note: ⚠⚠ NOT A PATRIARCH FOR MOST OF THIS: ch. 15's spine row has him as LOCUM TENENS of the patriarchate, burying the forty-four and rebuilding Golgotha, the Anastasis and the rest c.616-630. The lane carries him because the see was being administered, and the row says by whom and in what capacity.

rows.name: Sophronius I
rows.note: ⭐⭐ The patriarch of the surrender. ch. 15's spine rows already carry his Christmas sermon of 634 and his death in 638 or 639.
⛔ A REAL VACANCY OF TWO GENERATIONS after Sophronius, stated as such by Gil sec. 684 -- not a hole in the record and not an unbuilt stretch. This is what a `gap` row is for.

rows.name: Anastasius
rows.note: ⭐⭐⭐ NOTE THE 53-YEAR HOLE BEFORE HIM -- it is a REAL VACANCY, not a defect in the record. Gil sec. 684: "The patriarchal seat was vacant for a period of two generations... following the death of Sophronius", with some holding that Theodore bishop of Heshbon served in his stead.

rows.name: Elias II
rows.note: ⚠ ch. 18's spine row already has the civil-war devastation of 788 "under the patriarch Elias II" -- Gil's span covers it.

rows.name: Menas
rows.note: Gil gives him eight months.

rows.name: Simeon II
rows.note: ⚠⚠⚠ THREE AUTHORITIES, THREE DIFFERENT MEN'S WORTH OF DISAGREEMENT, AND THEY ARE ALL THIS ONE MAN. ⭐⭐ HE WAS ENTERED TWICE IN THIS FILE -- once from Gil as "Simeon II" and once from Pringle/Hamilton as "Symeon II" -- and the duplicate was invisible to the validator and OBVIOUS ON THE RENDERED PAGE, where two labels sat eight years apart in the same lane. Merged 2026-08-12. THE SPELLING SPLIT IS WHY THE DUPLICATE SURVIVED: a file keyed on names cannot see that Simeon and Symeon are one person. ⚠⚠ GIL ENDS HIM IN 1096 and puts EUTHYMIUS in the see to 15 July 1099, where Hamilton, Pringle and the book have him to 1099 -- see the Euthymius (1096) row. ✅ SPELLING RULED 2026-08-12: SIMEON, both books. Hamilton 20/20 Symeon, Gil 5/5 Simeon, MacEvitt inconsistent within one book -- the chapters had inherited whichever source they leaned on.

rows.name: Euthymius
rows.note: ⚠⚠⚠ GIL PUTS EUTHYMIUS IN THE SEE FROM 1096 TO 15 JULY 1099 -- the day Jerusalem fell -- WHERE HAMILTON, PRINGLE AND THE BOOK HAVE SYMEON/SIMEON II. Read from the page image, not the text layer. ⭐ The likeliest reconciliation is that they are tracking DIFFERENT THINGS: Gil's list runs to the fall of the city and may follow the patriarch IN JERUSALEM, while Hamilton follows the man in EXILE IN CYPRUS, whom ch. 20 n. 3 has fleeing "the oppression of the Artukid Turks". ⛔ THAT IS A HYPOTHESIS AND IS NOT ASSERTED. It needs Gil sec. 684ff read properly before any chapter changes. NOTHING in the book should move until it is.

rows.name: Arnulf of Chocques (elect, not consecrated)
rows.note: Elected and never consecrated; both authorities say so in the same words. ⚠ ch. 20's spine row already carries his expulsion of the eastern Christians.

rows.name: John VIII
rows.note: ⭐⭐⭐ THE CASE THAT PROVES THE METHOD. Hamilton claims NO tenure -- floruit means only that the man is attested in that year. Pringle prints a range. The range is Pringle's reconstruction presented as data in a table that names Hamilton as its source.

rows.name: Arnulf of Chocques
rows.note: His second tenure, this time consecrated.

rows.name: Sabas
rows.note: Hamilton again gives a floruit and no tenure.

rows.name: Warmund of Picquigny
rows.note: ⚠ Hamilton's text layer renders the start as "Piis" -- read from the page, it is 1118.

rows.name: Nicolas
rows.note: The closest the Greek lane comes to agreement, and it still is not one: Pringle's "before 1122" against Hamilton's "c1122". ⚠ SPELLING: Pringle Nicolas, Hamilton Nicholas.

rows.name: John IX
rows.note: Pringle's end carries his own question mark. Hamilton gives a floruit and no tenure.

rows.name: Nicephorus II
rows.note: The ends are five years apart and neither is given as firm.

rows.name: Leontius II
rows.note: ⭐⭐⭐ THE ONE GREEK PATRIARCH WHO REACHED JERUSALEM in the whole century, in 1177-8, to "a cool reception from the Latin establishment" -- so the most load-bearing name in the stretch. ✅ THE NUMERAL IS AGREED: both authorities say Leontius II and the book is CORRECT. ⚠⚠ A first pass of this pilot reported Hamilton as saying Leontius I and RAISED IT AS A DEFECT IN THE BOOK. That was wrong: it came from Hamilton's PDF text layer, which renders the line "Leontius I = 1174/5-1184/5", and the "I =" is the second I plus spacing. The page image settles it. Withdrawn 2026-08-11. ⚠ The DATES still disagree by two years at the start and one at the end.

rows.name: Heraclius
rows.note: ⚠ ch. 22's spine rows carry him stripping the edicule before the surrender and leaving with the treasure.

rows.name: Dositheus I
rows.note: Ends agree; starts are two years and a hedge apart. ⭐⭐⭐ Pa: PAPADOPOULOS (1910, printed p. 407, read from the ANEMI page image) GIVES A THIRD AND BETTER-EXPLAINED ACCOUNT: he did not die -- he was TRANSLATED to the throne of Constantinople in 1191 by the Emperor Isaac Angelos, and the translation was held ANTICANONICAL, which is why the lists disagree about when he ceased at Jerusalem. Same mechanism as Nicodemus seven centuries later: an END-DATE in a list is compressing a translation, and the compression is where the disagreement comes from.

rows.name: Mark II Cataphlorus
rows.note: Pringle leaves the end open with a question mark; Hamilton gives "post 1195" and the surname. ⭐ After Saladin's conquest the Greek patriarchate is re-established IN THE CITY and the Greeks regain their churches (Pringle, same entry) -- the exile ends here. ⭐⭐ Pa: Papadopoulos p. 407 confirms the surname and supplies the event Pringle and Hamilton only imply -- he was ELECTED PATRIARCH OF JERUSALEM IN DOSITHEOS'S PLACE (Πατριάρχης δὲ Ἱεροσολύμων ἀντ' αὐτοῦ ἐξελέγη ὁ ΜΑΡΚΟΣ Β΄ Κατάφλωρος) after the scandal of the translation, the Emperor convening a synod on 3 SEPTEMBER 1191. ⚠ That is two years later than the 1189/90 both other authorities give, and it is a THIRD reading, not a tiebreak.

⛔ A HOLE THAT IS DATA. Hamilton runs Mark II to "post 1195" and names no successor before Euthymius, who "died at Sinai in 1222". Pringle's table jumps from Mark II to Euthymius II. NEVER INTERPOLATE ACROSS THIS.

rows.name: Aimery the Monk
rows.note: ⚠ The Latin patriarch now normally resides at ACRE, not Jerusalem. ch. 23's spine row carries the state of his church at his death.

rows.name: Albert of Vercelli
rows.note: Hamilton adds "St".

rows.name: Euthymius
rows.auth2: H: Euthymius, died at Sinai in 1222
rows.note: ⭐⭐ EIGHT YEARS APART ON A DEATH, and they disagree on the numeral too. Pringle gives no start at all.

rows.name: Gerold of Lausanne
rows.note: ⚠ ch. 22's spine row has Frederick II entering Jerusalem in March 1229 under his treaty with al-Kamil.

rows.name: Athanasius II
rows.note: ⭐ ch. 22's spine row already has the Holy Sepulchre "left largely in the hands of the Orthodox patriarch, Athanasius II" in 1231-1244 -- which follows Pringle. Hamilton gives one attested year.

rows.name: Robert of Nantes
rows.note: ⭐ ch. 22's spine row has him writing to Innocent IV from Acre in September 1244. Pringle notes he "may have visited the city briefly in 1244".

rows.name: James Pantaleon
rows.note: ⚠ Hamilton only past 1244 -- Pringle's table stops. SINGLE AUTHORITY: the `bar` here rests on Hamilton alone and a second must be found before it ships as a span.

rows.name: William II of Agen
rows.note: ⚠ Single authority, as above.

rows.name: Thomas Agni of Lentino
rows.note: ⚠ Single authority, as above.

rows.name: Gregory I
rows.note: Hamilton alone, and hedged at both ends.

rows.name: Elias of Perigueux
rows.note: ⚠ Single authority; Hamilton's own end is 87/8.

rows.name: Nicholas of Hanapes
rows.note: ⚠ Single authority. ⭐ He is the last Latin patriarch of the kingdom: ch. 23 is the fall of Acre, 18 May 1291.

rows.name: Thaddaeus
rows.note: Hamilton alone, one attested year.

rows.name: Lazaros
rows.note: ✅ CORROBORATED BY SIMAIOS, who numbers him the 102nd (printed ρζ´, a misprint for ρβ´) and gives him 32 years and the crowning of John Kantakouzenos at Adrianople. ⭐⭐ THE FIRST NAME IN THE 1296-1787 HOLE, and it comes from Papadopoulos printed p. 425 read from the ANEMI page image. Elected patriarch after 1334, he went to Constantinople for confirmation of his election by Andronikos III (1328-1341) as custom required -- and IN HIS ABSENCE a monk named Gerasimos laid slanders against him, got himself elected in his place, and went to the capital for confirmation in turn. ⚠ No end date. ⚠⚠ This row does NOT close the hole; it is one name inside a 491-year gap and the validator still reports the gap on either side of it.

rows.name: Gerasimos (rival)
rows.note: ⚠⚠ A RIVAL, NOT A SUCCESSOR, and recorded because a succession that suppresses its contested elections is not the thing this band is for. The monk who slandered Lazaros in his absence and was elected against him. Andronikos III did not recognise the usurpation outright but 'was not wholly disbelieving' of it. Papadopoulos printed p. 425.

rows.name: Lazarus (CV)
rows.note: ⭐ Le Quien's CV = Simaios's 102. ⭐⭐ AND HE DATES HIM WHERE SIMAIOS DOES NOT: 'Lazarus his predecessor was still alive in the year 1367' -- used as an argument against Dositheos's chronology, which is how the date survives.

rows.name: Markos
rows.note: ⚠⚠ NOT Le Quien's Marcus III, who sits more than a century later and comes from a Latin source. Same name, different man, different tradition. ⚠⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY. Simaios gives a tenure LENGTH and no year, and THE CHAIN DOES NOT CLOSE on the anchors either side, which is the finding of step 2 and not a defect in this row. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Sophronius IV (CVI)
rows.auth1: LQ: CVI; Dositheos's catalogue calls him the 110TH
rows.note: ⚠⚠ A THIRD NUMBERING SITS INSIDE THIS ROW. Le Quien reports that Dositheos's catalogue makes him the 110th and assigns him 46 years -- and then REFUSES it: 'at non video quomodo id verum sit', I do not see how that can be true, since Lazarus his predecessor was still alive in 1367. ⭐ Le Quien adjudicating his own source, in print, in 1740.

rows.name: Euthymios
rows.note: ⭐ Simaios knows him ONLY FROM A TROPARION in the two hymnographic canons of the patriarchs of Jerusalem, and says so. ⚠⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY. Simaios gives a tenure LENGTH and no year, and THE CHAIN DOES NOT CLOSE on the anchors either side, which is the finding of step 2 and not a defect in this row. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Dorotheus I (CVII)
rows.auth1: LQ: CVII; confirmed by John Palaiologos
rows.note: Confirmed by the Emperor John Palaiologos, who gave up the empire in 1384 or 1387 and died in 1391. ⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY — Le Quien gives no year here; placed between the anchors he does give. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Athanasios
rows.note: ⭐⭐ COMPOSED HOMILIES IN ARABIC, spiritually beneficial, for every Sunday and feast, read aloud to the pious. A direct datum for the book's Arabic-liturgy thread and one of the earliest. ⚠⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY. Simaios gives a tenure LENGTH and no year, and THE CHAIN DOES NOT CLOSE on the anchors either side, which is the finding of step 2 and not a defect in this row. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Theophilus II (CVIII)
rows.note: ⭐⭐ 'Hic Theophilus, DOROTHEI FILIUS, cui et successit in sede Hierosolymitana' -- son succeeding father in the see. Flourished under Manuel Palaiologos (from 1384/87) and his son John, who was reigning in 1419. ⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY — Le Quien gives no year here; placed between the anchors he does give. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Ioakeim
rows.note: ⭐ = Le Quien's CX Joachim, who held the see at the Council of Florence and whose vicars there were Mark of Ephesus and Dositheos of Monembasia. ⚠⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY. Simaios gives a tenure LENGTH and no year, and THE CHAIN DOES NOT CLOSE on the anchors either side, which is the finding of step 2 and not a defect in this row. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Theophanes II (CIX)
rows.note: ⚠ One of the 'duplex Theophanes' Le Quien notes at CXV -- of the two Theophanes in Dositheos's catalogue, one is missing who sat after Joachim. ⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY — Le Quien gives no year here; placed between the anchors he does give. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Joachim (CX)
rows.auth1: LQ: CX; at the Council of Florence, promoted 1440
rows.note: ⭐⭐ Held the see at the time of the Florentine synod; his vicars there were MARK OF EPHESUS and Dositheos of Monembasia, who subscribed the decree of union 'holding the place of the most holy Patriarch of Jerusalem, Lord Joachim'. ⚠ Le Quien adds that Joachim was so far from ratifying it that he overturned whatever had been done at Florence. = Simaios's 106 Ioakeim (40 years).

rows.name: Theophanes III (CXI)
rows.note: Associated with the Constantinople synod against the Florentine union. ⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY — Le Quien gives no year here; placed between the anchors he does give. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Gregorios
rows.note: ⭐⭐ AN ANCHOR THAT LANDS INSIDE ITS OWN SPAN: he went to Mehmed the Conqueror and received a chrysobull in the Hijra year 861 -- 1456/7 -- confirming the covenant of Umar ibn al-Khattab and the later decrees the Arab sultans had given the patriarchs. The placement was set from the tenure length and the anchor falls within it, which is corroboration rather than construction.

rows.name: Abraham (CXII)
rows.auth1: LQ: CXII; ⛔ NOT IN THE GREEK SOURCES
rows.note: ⭐⭐⭐ THE FIRST OF THE THREE THAT EXPLAIN THE WHOLE DIVERGENCE. Le Quien states it outright: 'Licet nulla occurrat apud Graecos, de tribus istis Patriarchis Hierosolymorum mentio' -- NO MENTION OF THESE THREE OCCURS AMONG THE GREEKS. He takes them from THEODORICUS PAULI by way of Papebrochius. Theodoricus calls Abraham a most Christian man who governed the church of Jerusalem under the greatest pressure of the pagans, in the time of Pope Pius II, and who died in 1468.

rows.name: Jacobus III (CXIII)
rows.auth1: LQ: CXIII; ⛔ NOT IN THE GREEK SOURCES
rows.note: The second of the three from Theodoricus Pauli: 'doctor of sacred page, succeeding Abraham, and in great want governing the patriarchate'; the Duke of Burgundy's help renovated the church of the Holy Sepulchre and sent a yearly sum. Died 1482.

rows.name: Marcus III (CXIV)
rows.auth1: LQ: CXIV; ⛔ NOT IN THE GREEK SOURCES
rows.note: The third from Theodoricus Pauli: 'Marcus, catholic and pious, by divine mercy archbishop of Bethlehem and Patriarch of the holy city of Jerusalem and of holy Sion, of Syria and Arabia and beyond Jordan'. ⚠⚠ DO NOT CONFUSE HIM WITH SIMAIOS'S 103 MARKOS, who sits more than a century earlier. Same name, different man, different tradition -- and that pair was what first made the two lists look irreconcilable. ⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY — Le Quien gives no year here; placed between the anchors he does give. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Atallas or Dorotheos
rows.note: ⭐⭐⭐ THE ROW THAT PROVES THE TWO LISTS ARE ONE SUCCESSION: Simaios gives him 43 years and Le Quien's CXVI Dorotheus II is given 43 years by Dositheos. The same man, the same tenure, in both traditions. ⭐ And the anchor lands inside the span: in 1514 Selim took Aleppo, Damascus and Jerusalem, and Dorotheos went out to receive him with gifts.

rows.name: Gregorius III (CXV)
rows.note: Le Quien reasons him into place: of the two Theophanes one is missing after Joachim, and 'it is likely that Gregory III succeeded the three just recited', to whom Dositheos assigns thirty-six years. ⚠ An inference of Le Quien's own, and he says so.

rows.name: Dorotheus II (CXVI)
rows.note: ⭐⭐ THE ROW THAT PROVES THE ALIGNMENT: Dositheos assigns him FORTY-THREE years, and Simaios gives his 108th, Atallas or Dorotheos, FORTY-THREE years. The same man, in both traditions, with the same tenure. ⭐ Le Quien adds that he must therefore have lived into the sixteenth century when it was already well advanced.

rows.name: Germanos
rows.note: ⭐ From Arachova in the Tripolitza country, formerly abbot of the Great Laura of St Sabas. Spent much of his time BEYOND THE JORDAN, 'for there were many multitudes of Orthodox Christians there'. ⚠⚠ The 46 years and the anchor at Adam 7086 (1578) do not close on the death at Adam 7116 (1608) -- thirty years, not forty-six. Recorded as it stands. = Le Quien CXVII.

rows.name: Germanus (CXVII)
rows.note: = Simaios's 109 Germanos, and the point where the two lists rejoin at the standing offset of 8. ⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY — Le Quien gives no year here; placed between the anchors he does give. The mark is `point`.

rows.name: Sophronios
rows.note: ⭐ GERMANOS'S OWN NEPHEW, a priest whom his uncle clothed in the monastic habit, renamed, and designated successor before dying. ⚠ Simaios gives him 38 or 39 years before he gave way, aged, to Theophanes -- which does not fit between 1608 and Paisios's 1645, and the row does not pretend it does.

rows.name: Theophanes III
rows.auth1: Si: 111; ordained by Alexandria and Antioch
rows.note: ⭐ Ordained by Kyrillos of Alexandria and Dorotheos of Antioch. This is the Theophanes III of ch. 25's 1637 spine row -- the patriarch of the Holy Fire disputes with the Armenians and of the long debt. ⚠⚠ HIS PLACEMENT IS THE WORST IN THE BAND: Simaios's chain puts Sophronios's 38 or 39 years before him and Paisios's consecration after him, and the two do not leave him room. Shown as a point at the join, with the problem stated rather than absorbed.

rows.name: Paisios
rows.auth1: Si: consecrated in Moldavia, 23 March, from Adam 7153 or 7157; 18 years
rows.note: ⭐ Simaios's 112th. Consecrated **in Moldavia**, 23 March on a Lenten Sunday, by Gregorios of Larissa as exarch of Parthenios of Constantinople, with Varlaam of Moldavia and a third bishop. ⚠ The Adam-year is given as EITHER 7153 or 7157 — 1645 or 1649 — so the start is a point, not a span; the 18 years closes on Nektarios's 1664 from the earlier of the two. ⭐⭐ Simaios describes him: 'without possessions, zealous in divine things, brave and strong in body, short of stature, deep-bearded, dark-complexioned, from Demetsana, a relative of Theophanes.' ✅ Le Quien has him as CXX at the standing offset of 8.

rows.name: Nektarios
rows.note: ⭐⭐ THE FIRST ROW IN THIS STRETCH WITH BOTH ENDS GIVEN AS AD YEARS BY THE SOURCE ITSELF. The Sinaite; came from Egypt to Gaza and met Gabriel of Philippoupolis at Ramla; consecrated in Jerusalem on Palm Sunday 1664 (from Adam 7174), and resigned the throne in 1669. ✅ Le Quien CXXI, offset 8. ⚠ `bar1` and not `bar` because Le Quien's own dates were not extracted — only his name and position.

rows.name: Dositheos II
rows.auth1: Si: from 1669; died 7 February 1707, patriarch 37 years
rows.note: ⭐⭐ From **Arachova of Corinth**. Found the throne's debt at 81,000 grosia and raised 20,000 in Greece and Wallachia-Moldavia, bringing back forty silver lamps, one gold, and a gold censer. ⭐ THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES ON ITSELF: Nektarios resigns 1669, Dositheos dies 7 Feb 1707, and Simaios says 37 years — 1669 + 37 = 1706/7. **This is why the Ottoman half could be written and the Byzantine half could not.** ✅ Le Quien CXXII. ⚠ He is also the compiler of the CATALOGUE Le Quien cites and argues with.

rows.name: Chrysanthos
rows.auth1: Si: translated from Caesarea 8 February 1707; 25 years
rows.note: ⭐ Dositheos's nephew, translated from Caesarea of Palestine the day after his uncle's death. ⭐⭐ Under him the synodal act of **April 1709** lists the whole hierarchy by see — metropolitans of Caesarea of Palestine, Skythopolis, Petra, Ptolemais, Bethlehem, Nazareth and Sebasteia; archbishops of Lydda, Gaza, Sinai, Joppa, Neapolis-and-Samaria and Thabor; and one bishop, of Philadelphia. ⚠ The end is from Simaios's stated 25 years, not from a stated year. ✅ Le Quien CXXIII.

rows.name: Meletios
rows.auth1: Si: to 1737, when he named a successor; start from Chrysanthos's 25 years
rows.note: ⭐ Simaios: 'being old and unable to relieve the debt, he appointed a successor in his own place' in 1737. ⚠ The START is not stated — it follows from Chrysanthos's 25 years — and the row says so rather than hiding it. ✅ Le Quien CXXIV is the last entry his 1740 volume reaches; **from here Simaios is the only authority.**

rows.name: Parthenios
rows.note: ⭐ Of ATHENS. Under him the church of the Annunciation at Nazareth was rebuilt from the foundations by the archimandrite Neophytos of Rhodes. ⚠⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY, AND THE METHOD IS STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISTAKEN FOR EVIDENCE: Simaios gives him no year. He is placed by dividing the interval between the two FIRM anchors either side of him among the men who fill it. The mark is `point`; the start and end are for the axis and are never a claim.

rows.name: Ephraim II
rows.note: ⭐ Of ATHENS. Died and was buried at Constantinople, and his relics were afterwards translated to Jerusalem. ⚠⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY, AND THE METHOD IS STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISTAKEN FOR EVIDENCE: Simaios gives him no year. He is placed by dividing the interval between the two FIRM anchors either side of him among the men who fill it. The mark is `point`; the start and end are for the axis and are never a claim.

rows.name: Sophronios
rows.note: ⭐⭐ THE TRAFFIC RUNS BOTH WAYS: he went UP from Jerusalem to the throne of Constantinople in 1770, and in the same year named his own successor at Jerusalem. ⚠ Only the END year is given; the start is placement between the anchors.

rows.name: Abramios
rows.note: Laboured in Wallachia-Moldavia gathering money for the throne, as Dositheos had. ⚠⚠ PLACEMENT ONLY, AND THE METHOD IS STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISTAKEN FOR EVIDENCE: Simaios gives him no year. He is placed by dividing the interval between the two FIRM anchors either side of him among the men who fill it. The mark is `point`; the start and end are for the axis and are never a claim.

rows.name: Prokopios
rows.auth1: Si: one year; from Caesarea of Palestine
rows.note: ⚠ Simaios gives him ONE YEAR and no anchor; he is placed against Anthimos's stated 1787, which is the firm year on the other side. From Caesarea of Palestine and resident at Constantinople, where he was buried; he named his own successor.

rows.name: Anthimus
rows.note: ⚠⚠ BOTH READINGS NOW PAGE-VERIFIED AND THEY DISAGREE AT BOTH ENDS: Dowling 1787-1808 against the Handbook 1788-1807. ⭐ A WebFetch summary of Dowling's page had claimed 1807-1808 -- wrong by twenty years, and invented. Neither real reading is that.

rows.name: Polycarp
rows.note: ✅ The two authorities agree exactly. ⭐⭐ THE FIRST AGREED SPAN IN THE JERUSALEM LANE IN THE WHOLE BAND -- 79 entries from James onward and not one before this.

rows.name: Athanasius V
rows.note: ✅ The DATES agree exactly, so this is a bar. ⚠⚠ THE NUMERAL DOES NOT: Dowling has ATHANASIUS V here and again in his Bethlehem list; the Handbook prints ATHANASIOS IV. Both page-verified. A regnal number is not a date and does not change the mark -- it goes here, unresolved.

rows.name: Kyrillus II
rows.note: ✅ Agreed. ⭐ Dowling calls him the 128TH PATRIARCH, the anchor for the numbering question at Damianus. Deposed, per Dowling.

rows.name: Procopius II
rows.note: ⚠ Two years apart at the end: Dowling 1875 and 'Resigned', the Handbook 1877. Dowling's earlier end leaves a vacancy the Handbook fills.

rows.name: Heirotheus
rows.note: ⚠ FOUR years apart at the start -- Dowling 1875, the Handbook 1879 -- which is the same disagreement seen from the other side: the Handbook has a 1877-1879 vacancy where Dowling has Heirotheus in office from 1875.

rows.name: Nicodemus
rows.note: ⚠ A year out at both ends. ⭐⭐ AND THE BOOK IS VINDICATED: ch. 27 follows Bliss in dating the cry that forced him out to 1891, which had looked like a third disagreement. Dowling's own p. 26 footnote resolves it -- Nicodemus resigns 1890, the throne stands empty a year, and Gerasimus is TRANSLATED from Antioch in 1891. The lists compress a resignation, a vacancy and a translation into one number; the book described the EVENT, not the tenure.

rows.name: Gerasimus
rows.note: ⚠ Dowling 1891, the Handbook 1890, both page-verified -- and Dowling's footnote naming the 1891 translation from Antioch makes his the better-evidenced reading. The book follows the same year.

rows.name: Damianus
rows.note: ⭐ Both leave the end open; the 1931 here is ch. 28's spine row, not either authority. ⚠⚠ OPEN QUESTION, page-verified and therefore real: Dowling calls him the 132ND PATRIARCH and Kyrillus II the 128th, but counting the list between them gives 133 -- one of the five is outside the official numbering, plausibly one who resigned or the one deposed.
